newsitem.title: USA: Housing starts down in May for third straight month.
newsitem.headline: Housing starts down in May for third straight month.

text.p: Construction starts on new homes and apartments dropped for a third consecutive month in May, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, as the housing sector gradually lost some strength.

Total starts fell 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.397 million in May after revised declines of 0.7 percent in April and 4.8 percent in March. The figures still suggest a relatively solid housing market, supported by a steadily expanding economy, although building is expected to decline gradually in coming months from a boom pace at the beginning of the year.
The May building rate was the slowest since January and was weaker than anticipated by Wall Street analysts, who had forecast starts at a rate of 1.47 million a year.
Department officials said it was the first time that starts had fallen for three months in a row in more than two years, since the period from January through March 1995.
Industry analysts predict 1997 building peaked during the first quarter, when the rate reached 1.554 million a year during February amid exceptionally mild weather that benefited builders.
Previously, the department said April housing starts had risen 2.6 percent to 1.473 million a year and that March starts had fallen 7.7 percent to 1.435 million, but it revised both estimates.

While building activity is expected to ease, there is little likelihood of a major downturn for construction industries. Interest rates have fallen recently, further helping to bolster sales and construction in the rate-sensitive housing sector.

The National Association of Home Builders said on Monday that its index of market activity rose in June by two points to a level of 57. It said declining interest rates and favourable weather had stimulated building.

Construction starts on single-family homes fell 2.5 percent in May to a rate of 1.088 million after decreasing 2.3 percent in April. Starts on apartments plunged 12.2 percent during May to a rate of 309,000 following a 5.1 percent rise in April.
Mortage rates eased in May from April. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.93 percent in May, down from 8.14 percent in April.
Rates have continued to fall, and rates for a long-term loan in mid-June were at their lowest since February.
Total starts during May were 5.4 percent lower than in May 1996, when homes were being built at a rate of 1.476 million a year.
Regionally, starts fell everywhere except in the West, where they rose 5.2 percent to an annual rate of 365,000.

Starts dropped 11.3 percent in the South, the nation's largest regional market, to an annual rate of 615,000. In the Northeast, starts declined 8.1 percent during May to 124,000 a year, while in the Midwest they were unchanged from April at an annual rate of 293,000.
